chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prayed Al-Maghrib with us, so he recited the two Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 113 & 114) in the two Rak'at.

key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 113 and 114 of the Quran)

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet or Imams recite the Mu'awwidhat in the Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of reciting the Mu'awwidhat (Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas) during the Maghrib prayer, specifically in the first two rak'at. It serves as a key juristic evidence (hujjah) in Shia fiqh for the permissibility and virtue of incorporating these protective chapters into obligatory prayers, reflecting the Imam's emphasis on spiritual protection through Quranic recitation. The chain of transmission via Safwan al-Jammal underscores the reliability of this practice within the early Shia scholarly tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws prayed Al Maghrib Salāt with us, so heasws recited with the Mawazatayn (Chapters 113 & 114) during the two Rak’at’ (Rak’ats).
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from af-Husayn ibn abu Najran from Safwan al-Jammai who has said the foiiowing: “
Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once led us in al-Maghrib Salah (prayer) and recited al- Ma’udhatayn in two Rak’at.”
